title: Find the newest file
hook: Sorting by size answers a different question from sorting by date.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: that size and date are separate, so the latest file is found by sorting on modified date

misconception: The biggest file is usually the latest version.
objective: Choose sorting metadata that matches the retrieval goal.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: Sorting by size answers a different question from sorting by date. To find the most recently modified file, which sort fits? Correct option: Modified day. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data. The stage caption reads: d = day modified; higher = more recent.

claims.text: Size and name do not record when a file changed; sort by the field that answers the question.
claims.source: Recall item for this lesson: stipulated example data and the rule taught in the lesson (company/reviews/lifehacks-200/recall-patch-study.md + recall-patch-study.lines.txt). Applies to the example only; no empirical effect is claimed. Recall patch by learning-designer (session 2, 2026-10-14), applied by session 1. Pointer corrected by demo-builder 2026-10-14 (W-391a). | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Convention and logic: size and name fields are not modification timestamps, so sorting by them need not put the last-changed file first; the fixture shows it: by size movie (90MB, d1), slides, notes; by day notes (d9), slides, movie (own node, same as fileResult "sort"). The keyed option (index 2, "Date modified, newest first") is the only field that records change time.

recall.question: You want the last file you worked on. Which sort puts it on top?
recall.why: Size and name do not record when a file changed; sort by the field that answers the question.
